scr_jobcost_lien_releases_list.purpose: Lists lien releases (waivers) generated or received for job cost payments — contractor, job, amount covered, conditional or unconditional, status — so every payment has its waiver on file.
scr_jobcost_lien_releases_list.outcome: A register proving that paid contractors and suppliers have waived lien rights for the amounts paid.
scr_jobcost_lien_releases_list.rootCause: State mechanics' lien laws let unpaid contractors, subcontractors and suppliers lien the property. Lenders and title insurers require waivers for each payment; the list is how the accountant confirms none are missing before a draw or a sale.
scr_jobcost_lien_releases_list.ifSkipped: Missing waivers surface when a lien is filed, a draw is rejected or a sale closing is delayed by a title exception.
redFlags: Payments without unconditional waivers after the check cleared
Waivers from the GC but none from lower-tier subs

scr_jobcost_generating_a_lien_release_pa.purpose: Generates a package of lien release documents for selected job payments, merged from templates with vendor, amount, job and date details, ready for contractors to sign.
scr_jobcost_generating_a_lien_release_pa.outcome: Correctly completed waiver forms issued with each payment, reducing back-and-forth with contractors.
scr_jobcost_generating_a_lien_release_pa.rootCause: Many states prescribe statutory waiver forms (conditional on progress payment, unconditional on final payment). Generating them from payment data avoids errors in amounts and dates that make waivers invalid.
scr_jobcost_generating_a_lien_release_pa.ifSkipped: Waivers are prepared by hand with wrong amounts or forms and may not protect the owner.
gaap: State statutory lien waiver forms (e.g., CA Civil Code §8132-8138, TX Property Code §53.284)
redFlags: Unconditional waivers issued before payment clears

scr_jobcost_creating_and_uploading_a_lie.purpose: Creates a Word lien release template with merge fields and uploads it so the system can generate waivers in the state-required format.
scr_jobcost_creating_and_uploading_a_lie.outcome: State-compliant waiver templates available for every property's jurisdiction.
scr_jobcost_creating_and_uploading_a_lie.rootCause: Statutory waiver language varies by state and non-compliant forms may be unenforceable. Templates encode the correct language once for reuse.
scr_jobcost_creating_and_uploading_a_lie.ifSkipped: Waivers use generic language that may not protect the owner in statutory-form states.
redFlags: One template used for properties in states with statutory forms

scr_jobcost_downloading_and_installing_t.purpose: Downloads and installs the Word Merge tool used to insert RealPage merge fields into lien release and other document templates.
scr_jobcost_downloading_and_installing_t.outcome: Template designers can build merge-enabled documents.
scr_jobcost_downloading_and_installing_t.rootCause: Merge fields must be inserted with the tool for templates to populate correctly from payment data.
scr_jobcost_downloading_and_installing_t.ifSkipped: Templates cannot be built or maintained, and waivers are prepared manually.
redFlags: Templates edited without the tool, breaking merge fields

scr_jobcost_logging_in_to_the_word_merge.purpose: Logs in to the Word Merge tool with RealPage credentials so templates can be linked to the company's data fields.
scr_jobcost_logging_in_to_the_word_merge.outcome: The tool is connected to the company's field definitions.
scr_jobcost_logging_in_to_the_word_merge.rootCause: Merge fields are company-specific; the tool must connect to the right company to offer valid fields.
scr_jobcost_logging_in_to_the_word_merge.ifSkipped: Templates reference invalid fields and generate blank documents.
redFlags: Shared credentials used for the tool

scr_jobcost_choosing_a_word_file_for_you.purpose: Selects the Word file that will become a document template, such as the state's statutory waiver form.
scr_jobcost_choosing_a_word_file_for_you.outcome: The correct base document is used for the template.
scr_jobcost_choosing_a_word_file_for_you.rootCause: Starting from the official statutory form ensures the template's legal language is correct before merge fields are added.
scr_jobcost_choosing_a_word_file_for_you.ifSkipped: Templates are built from outdated or non-compliant forms.
redFlags: Templates based on superseded statutory forms

scr_jobcost_using_the_word_merge_tool_to.purpose: Inserts merge fields (vendor, amount, job, property, dates) into the Word template.
scr_jobcost_using_the_word_merge_tool_to.outcome: Templates populate automatically with payment details.
scr_jobcost_using_the_word_merge_tool_to.rootCause: Accurate field placement guarantees that the amount and date on each waiver match the payment it covers — the key requirement for a valid waiver.
scr_jobcost_using_the_word_merge_tool_to.ifSkipped: Waiver amounts or dates are typed manually and may not match payments.
redFlags: Amount fields mapped to invoice total instead of payment amount

scr_jobcost_syncing_a_document_template_.purpose: Syncs a finished Word template back to RealPage Accounting so it is available for generating documents.
scr_jobcost_syncing_a_document_template_.outcome: Updated templates are live for waiver generation.
scr_jobcost_syncing_a_document_template_.rootCause: Template changes (a statutory form update) have no effect until synced; unsynced templates leave users generating the old version.
scr_jobcost_syncing_a_document_template_.ifSkipped: Waivers continue to be generated on outdated templates.

scr_jobcost_setting_up_job_cost_and_rese.purpose: Section on setting up Job Cost & Reserves — configuration, permits, segments, cost structures, job types, cost codes, reserve schedules, reporting codes, draw models and funding sources.
scr_jobcost_setting_up_job_cost_and_rese.outcome: A configured project accounting structure ready for jobs and draws.
scr_jobcost_setting_up_job_cost_and_rese.rootCause: Every draw and project report depends on this setup; building it thoughtfully once avoids restructuring projects mid-flight.
scr_jobcost_setting_up_job_cost_and_rese.ifSkipped: Projects are set up inconsistently and draws must be reformatted manually for each lender.
redFlags: Setup not aligned with lender draw formats

scr_jobcost_configuration.purpose: The Configuration section of Job Cost & Reserves setup, controlling application-wide settings such as integrations, budget checks and default accounts.
scr_jobcost_configuration.outcome: Job cost behaves consistently with company policy.
scr_jobcost_configuration.rootCause: Settings such as whether budget checks block over-budget commitments determine how strong project controls are.
scr_jobcost_configuration.ifSkipped: Project controls operate inconsistently or not at all.

scr_jobcost_configure_job_cost_and_reser.purpose: The Configure page for Job Cost & Reserves where default accounts, integration options and control settings are set.
scr_jobcost_configure_job_cost_and_reser.outcome: Company-wide job cost settings defined in one place.
scr_jobcost_configure_job_cost_and_reser.rootCause: Default accounts (e.g., CIP, retainage payable) drive postings for every job; errors here misstate balance sheets across the portfolio.
scr_jobcost_configure_job_cost_and_reser.ifSkipped: Job postings hit wrong default accounts.

scr_jobcost_configuring_job_cost.purpose: Procedure for configuring Job Cost from Setup > Configuration — default CIP and retainage accounts, budget-check behavior, integration options — before the first job is created.
scr_jobcost_configuring_job_cost.outcome: Job cost configured before first use.
scr_jobcost_configuring_job_cost.rootCause: Every job created afterwards inherits these settings. Configuring first avoids reposting costs or restructuring jobs when a default (such as the retainage payable account) turns out to be wrong after projects are underway.
scr_jobcost_configuring_job_cost.ifSkipped: Jobs are created under defaults that later need correcting.
redFlags: Configuration changed after jobs exist without review

scr_jobcost_integrating_job_cost_with_pr.purpose: Sets up the integration between RealPage Job Cost and Procore so jobs, budgets, commitments and costs flow between them.
scr_jobcost_integrating_job_cost_with_pr.outcome: Construction and accounting work from synchronized project data.
scr_jobcost_integrating_job_cost_with_pr.rootCause: Construction teams live in Procore and accounting in RealPage; without integration, the two diverge and reconciliation becomes a monthly manual exercise.
scr_jobcost_integrating_job_cost_with_pr.ifSkipped: Project data diverges and draws are built on inconsistent figures.

scr_jobcost_permits.purpose: Explains permits — categories used to organize job attachments such as building permits, inspection certificates and certificates of occupancy.
scr_jobcost_permits.outcome: Regulatory documents for projects are organized and retrievable.
scr_jobcost_permits.rootCause: Lenders and municipalities require proof of permits and inspections for capital work; organizing them by category makes them available for draws and closeouts.
scr_jobcost_permits.ifSkipped: Permit documents are scattered and draws or closeouts are delayed.

scr_jobcost_permits_list.purpose: Lists the permit categories (building permit, electrical permit, final inspection, certificate of occupancy) used to classify documents attached to jobs.
scr_jobcost_permits_list.outcome: A consistent set of document categories across projects.
scr_jobcost_permits_list.rootCause: Consistent categories let anyone find a project's building permit or final inspection quickly during a draw or audit.
scr_jobcost_permits_list.ifSkipped: Documents are mislabeled and hard to find.

scr_jobcost_adding_a_permit.purpose: Adds a permit category for job attachments, for example 'Roofing Permit' or 'Final Inspection'.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_permit.outcome: New document types can be classified on jobs.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_permit.rootCause: New project types may require new permit categories so documents stay organized.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_permit.ifSkipped: New document types are filed under generic categories.

scr_jobcost_viewing_a_permit.purpose: Views a permit category's name and description to confirm which documents belong in it before filing a job attachment.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_permit.outcome: Clarity on how a category should be used.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_permit.rootCause: Users need to know what belongs in each category to file documents consistently.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_permit.ifSkipped: Permit documents are filed under the wrong category and cannot be found for a draw or closeout.

scr_jobcost_deleting_a_permit.purpose: Deletes a permit category that is no longer used, for example a category created for a one-off municipal inspection type.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_permit.rootCause: Unused permit categories clutter the selection list and lead staff to file building permits or inspection certificates under the wrong heading, which slows retrieval when a lender asks for them.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_permit.ifSkipped: Users misfile documents under obsolete categories.

scr_jobcost_permit_information_page.purpose: The permit category record page holding the category name and description that users select when attaching permits and inspection documents to jobs.
scr_jobcost_permit_information_page.outcome: A defined category for job documents.
scr_jobcost_permit_information_page.rootCause: Clear definitions support consistent document organization across properties and projects.
scr_jobcost_permit_information_page.ifSkipped: Categories are applied inconsistently and project documents are hard to retrieve.

scr_jobcost_segments.purpose: Explains job segments — the breakdown of a job into parts (cost codes, phases, buildings) against which budgets and costs are tracked.
scr_jobcost_segments.outcome: Projects are tracked at the level of detail owners and lenders need.
scr_jobcost_segments.rootCause: A $2M renovation cannot be managed as one number; segments let the team control each trade or phase separately.
scr_jobcost_segments.ifSkipped: Projects are tracked only in total and overruns in specific trades are hidden.

scr_jobcost_job_segments_list.purpose: Lists the job segments (cost codes, phases or buildings) set up in Job Cost & Reserves, with codes and descriptions, as the catalog used when defining segments on each job.
scr_jobcost_job_segments_list.outcome: A catalog of segments for consistent budgeting.
scr_jobcost_job_segments_list.rootCause: Reusing standard segments across jobs is what makes projects comparable — two roof jobs with the same segments can be benchmarked; two with ad hoc segments cannot.
scr_jobcost_job_segments_list.ifSkipped: Each job invents segments and comparisons fail.

scr_jobcost_defining_job_segments_for_a_.purpose: Defines which segments apply to a specific job — for example the trades involved in a roof replacement.
scr_jobcost_defining_job_segments_for_a_.outcome: The job has exactly the segments its scope requires.
scr_jobcost_defining_job_segments_for_a_.rootCause: Defining segments per job keeps budgets focused on the trades actually involved.
scr_jobcost_defining_job_segments_for_a_.ifSkipped: Jobs carry irrelevant segments or miss needed ones.
redFlags: Segments missing for trades in the contract

scr_jobcost_editing_a_job_segment.purpose: Edits a job segment's description or settings — for example renaming 'Phase 2' to 'Phase 2 — Buildings 5-8' so draws and reports are clearer.
scr_jobcost_editing_a_job_segment.rootCause: Segment names appear on draws and capex reports seen by lenders and owners. Unclear or outdated names cause questions and slow approvals.
scr_jobcost_editing_a_job_segment.ifSkipped: Draws and capex reports show confusing segment labels that lenders question.

scr_jobcost_viewing_a_job_segment.purpose: Views a job segment's details and the jobs using it, typically before changing or deleting it.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_job_segment.outcome: Understanding of how a segment is applied across jobs.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_job_segment.rootCause: A segment may be used on many jobs; changing it without seeing where it is used can alter active projects' budgets and draws unexpectedly.

scr_jobcost_job_segment_information_page.purpose: The job segment record page holding the segment code, description and settings that control how costs are grouped in job reports and draws.
scr_jobcost_job_segment_information_page.outcome: A complete definition of a segment.
scr_jobcost_job_segment_information_page.rootCause: Segment settings decide how costs group on job status reports and lender draws; a wrong setting misplaces costs in every report that uses the segment.
scr_jobcost_job_segment_information_page.ifSkipped: Costs group incorrectly on job reports and lender draws.

scr_jobcost_cost_structure_definition.purpose: Explains cost structures — the hierarchy that organizes cost codes into categories (e.g., hard costs > roofing > materials) for reporting and draws.
scr_jobcost_cost_structure_definition.outcome: Project costs roll up into categories lenders and owners recognize.
scr_jobcost_cost_structure_definition.rootCause: Lenders review draws in categories (hard costs, soft costs, contingency). A cost structure makes that roll-up automatic.
scr_jobcost_cost_structure_definition.ifSkipped: Costs must be re-categorized manually for each lender report.
redFlags: Structures inconsistent with lender budget categories

scr_jobcost_cost_structures_list.purpose: Lists cost structures — the hierarchies that roll cost codes up into categories such as hard costs, soft costs and contingency — with actions to add, duplicate, edit, view or delete.
scr_jobcost_cost_structures_list.outcome: Maintained cost hierarchies for different project types.
scr_jobcost_cost_structures_list.rootCause: Construction, renovation and reserve work may need different structures; the list manages them.
scr_jobcost_cost_structures_list.ifSkipped: One structure is forced on all project types.

scr_jobcost_adding_duplicating_or_editin.purpose: Adds a new cost structure, duplicates an existing one as a starting point, or edits a structure's hierarchy.
scr_jobcost_adding_duplicating_or_editin.outcome: Cost structures tailored to project types or lender formats.
scr_jobcost_adding_duplicating_or_editin.rootCause: A new lender or project type may need a variant structure; duplicating keeps the standard base.
scr_jobcost_adding_duplicating_or_editin.ifSkipped: Structures are rebuilt from scratch with inconsistencies.
redFlags: Edits to structures used by active jobs

scr_jobcost_viewing_a_cost_structure.purpose: Views a cost structure's hierarchy of categories and cost codes to understand how project costs roll up on reports and lender draws.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_cost_structure.outcome: Clarity on which category each cost code rolls into.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_cost_structure.rootCause: When a lender asks why a cost appears under soft costs instead of hard costs, the answer lies in the cost structure. Viewing it lets the accountant explain or correct the roll-up.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_cost_structure.ifSkipped: Draw categories cannot be explained to the lender and questioned items delay funding.

scr_jobcost_deleting_a_cost_structure.purpose: Deletes a cost structure that no job uses, such as a draft hierarchy that was replaced before go-live.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_cost_structure.rootCause: Obsolete cost structures remain selectable when new jobs are set up; choosing one produces reports and draws in a category layout no lender or owner expects.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_cost_structure.ifSkipped: New jobs are set up on obsolete structures.

scr_jobcost_cost_structure_information_p.purpose: The cost structure record page defining its hierarchy levels and which cost codes sit under each category.
scr_jobcost_cost_structure_information_p.outcome: A complete definition of a cost hierarchy.
scr_jobcost_cost_structure_information_p.rootCause: The hierarchy defined here drives every roll-up in job status reports and draws. A code placed under the wrong category misstates hard versus soft costs for every job using the structure.
scr_jobcost_cost_structure_information_p.ifSkipped: Roll-ups are wrong across all reports and draws that use the structure.

scr_jobcost_job_types.purpose: Explains job types — classifications (capex improvement, replacement reserve repair, construction, tenant improvement) that carry default GL accounts and cost codes.
scr_jobcost_job_types.outcome: Jobs inherit the right accounts and codes by type.
scr_jobcost_job_types.rootCause: Job type determines whether costs capitalize, which reserve can fund them, and what codes apply; setting it drives consistent accounting.
scr_jobcost_job_types.ifSkipped: Jobs use wrong accounts, for example reserve-eligible repairs posted as ordinary capex.
gaap: ASC 360-10 vs ASC 720 — capital vs expense
redFlags: Expense-type jobs posting to capital accounts

scr_jobcost_job_types_list.purpose: Lists job types (capital improvement, replacement reserve repair, ground-up construction, tenant improvement) with their default GL accounts and cost codes.
scr_jobcost_job_types_list.rootCause: Reviewing job types periodically ensures their default accounts still align with the capitalization policy and chart of accounts; outdated defaults silently misclassify every new job.
scr_jobcost_job_types_list.ifSkipped: New jobs inherit outdated defaults and post capital work to the wrong accounts.

scr_jobcost_adding_a_job_type.purpose: Adds a job type — for example 'EV Charger Installation' or 'Solar Retrofit' — with its default GL accounts for recording job costs and the cost codes that apply.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_job_type.outcome: A new project classification with correct accounting defaults.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_job_type.rootCause: New project kinds (e.g., EV charger installations) need types with correct capital accounts.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_job_type.ifSkipped: New kinds of projects post to generic accounts and cannot be reported as a category.

scr_jobcost_viewing_or_editing_a_job_typ.purpose: Views or edits a job type's default GL accounts and cost codes — typically after chart of accounts changes or a capitalization policy update.
scr_jobcost_viewing_or_editing_a_job_typ.rootCause: Chart of accounts changes require job type defaults to be updated or new jobs post to obsolete accounts.
scr_jobcost_viewing_or_editing_a_job_typ.ifSkipped: New jobs post to inactive or obsolete accounts.

scr_jobcost_deleting_a_job_type.purpose: Deletes a job type that no job uses, for example a type created during setup testing.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_job_type.outcome: Only current project classifications remain selectable.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_job_type.rootCause: Obsolete job types stay selectable for new jobs and apply outdated default accounts and cost codes, misclassifying new projects from their first cost.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_job_type.ifSkipped: New jobs inherit outdated defaults from obsolete types.

scr_jobcost_managing_cost_codes_for_a_jo.purpose: Manages which cost codes apply to a job type so new jobs of that type start with the right codes.
scr_jobcost_managing_cost_codes_for_a_jo.outcome: Consistent cost codes across jobs of the same type.
scr_jobcost_managing_cost_codes_for_a_jo.rootCause: Standardizing codes by job type makes projects of the same kind comparable, such as roof replacements across properties.
scr_jobcost_managing_cost_codes_for_a_jo.ifSkipped: Similar projects use different codes and cannot be compared.
redFlags: Job types with no cost codes

scr_jobcost_job_type_information_page.purpose: The job type record page with its name, default GL accounts (CIP, expense, retainage) and assigned cost codes.
scr_jobcost_job_type_information_page.outcome: A complete definition of the job type.
scr_jobcost_job_type_information_page.rootCause: Defaults on this page are copied to every new job of the type; a wrong default account here misposts the costs of every future project of that kind.
scr_jobcost_job_type_information_page.ifSkipped: Errors spread to all new jobs of that type.

scr_jobcost_cost_codes_list.purpose: Lists cost codes available to job types, used to track budgets and costs by trade.
scr_jobcost_cost_codes_list.outcome: A maintained catalog of cost codes.
scr_jobcost_cost_codes_list.rootCause: Cost codes are the backbone of project tracking; a clean list prevents duplicates and coding errors.
scr_jobcost_cost_codes_list.ifSkipped: Duplicate codes split costs and confuse reports.

scr_jobcost_adding_a_cost_code.purpose: Adds a cost code (e.g., 07-310 Shingle Roofing) to a job type for budget and cost tracking.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_cost_code.outcome: A new trade category available on jobs.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_cost_code.rootCause: New scopes of work — for example adding EV chargers to a renovation — need a cost code before they can be budgeted and tracked separately. Without one, the cost is coded to an unrelated trade and distorts that trade's budget.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_cost_code.ifSkipped: New scope is coded to unrelated trades and distorts their budgets.
redFlags: Codes not following the CSI MasterFormat convention used by the company

scr_jobcost_viewing_or_editing_a_cost_co.purpose: Views or edits a cost code's description and settings so site teams and accountants code invoices to the right trade.
scr_jobcost_viewing_or_editing_a_cost_co.rootCause: Vague cost code descriptions are a leading cause of mis-coded project invoices; clarifying them improves coding accuracy across every job that uses the code.
scr_jobcost_viewing_or_editing_a_cost_co.ifSkipped: Invoices continue to be mis-coded because the code's meaning is unclear.
redFlags: Edits changing meaning of codes with history

scr_jobcost_importing_cost_codes.purpose: Imports cost codes from a template, typically a standard code list such as CSI MasterFormat.
scr_jobcost_importing_cost_codes.outcome: A full code catalog loaded accurately.
scr_jobcost_importing_cost_codes.rootCause: Standard code lists such as CSI MasterFormat have hundreds of codes. Importing reproduces them exactly; keying them by hand introduces duplicates and typos that split costs across near-identical codes.
scr_jobcost_importing_cost_codes.ifSkipped: Cost codes are keyed by hand with duplicates and typos.

scr_jobcost_deleting_cost_codes.purpose: Deletes cost codes that no job budget or transaction uses, keeping the list that site teams choose from short and accurate.
scr_jobcost_deleting_cost_codes.outcome: The cost code list contains only codes that are actually used.
scr_jobcost_deleting_cost_codes.rootCause: Long lists of unused codes increase the chance of picking a wrong but similar-looking code when coding project invoices, which misstates trade budgets.
scr_jobcost_deleting_cost_codes.ifSkipped: Project invoices are coded to obsolete or wrong codes.

scr_jobcost_cost_code_information_page.purpose: The cost code record page holding the code, description and settings used whenever a budget line or invoice is coded to that trade.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_information_page.outcome: A complete definition of one cost code.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_information_page.rootCause: Consistent, clear definitions on this page are what allow many people across properties to code project costs the same way.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_information_page.ifSkipped: Coding becomes inconsistent across jobs and properties.

scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedule.purpose: Explains reserve account schedules — the schedule of required monthly deposits into a lender replacement reserve, and how deposits are tracked against it.
scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedule.outcome: Required reserve deposits tracked so the property stays compliant with its loan.
scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedule.rootCause: Loan documents set a monthly reserve deposit (often $250-$400 per unit per year). Missing deposits or incorrect amounts are covenant issues flagged by servicers.
scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedule.ifSkipped: Reserve deposits are not tracked against requirements and shortfalls are flagged by the servicer.

scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedules_li.purpose: Lists reserve account schedules by property and reserve with required deposits and effective dates.
scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedules_li.outcome: A portfolio view of reserve deposit obligations.
scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedules_li.rootCause: Deposit requirements change at loan modification or refinancing; the list keeps current obligations visible.

scr_jobcost_adding_a_reserve_account_sch.purpose: Adds a reserve deposit schedule for a property's reserve — monthly amount, start date and end date.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_reserve_account_sch.rootCause: Each loan's deposit terms must be recorded so actual deposits can be compared with requirements.
scr_jobcost_adding_a_reserve_account_sch.ifSkipped: Compliance with deposit terms cannot be tracked.

scr_jobcost_editing_a_reserve_account_sc.purpose: Edits a reserve account deposit schedule when the servicer changes the required monthly replacement reserve deposit after a loan modification or property reanalysis.
scr_jobcost_editing_a_reserve_account_sc.outcome: Deposit schedules match current loan terms.
scr_jobcost_editing_a_reserve_account_sc.rootCause: Loan modifications and servicer reanalysis change deposits; schedules must follow.

scr_jobcost_viewing_a_reserve_account_sc.purpose: Views a reserve account deposit schedule and its history of required monthly amounts, used when reconciling actual deposits to the servicer's statement.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_reserve_account_sc.outcome: Clarity on required deposits over time.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_reserve_account_sc.rootCause: Reconciling to servicer statements requires knowing the required deposit for each period.
scr_jobcost_viewing_a_reserve_account_sc.ifSkipped: Differences with servicer statements are not explained.

scr_jobcost_deleting_a_reserve_account_s.purpose: Deletes a reserve account deposit schedule that was created in error, such as a duplicate schedule for the same reserve and period.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_reserve_account_s.outcome: Only valid deposit schedules drive reserve compliance tracking.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_reserve_account_s.rootCause: A duplicate schedule doubles the required deposit shown for the reserve, so compliance tracking reports false shortfalls to the asset manager and servicer.

scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedule_inf.purpose: The reserve account schedule record page with deposit amount, frequency and dates.
scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedule_inf.outcome: A complete definition of the deposit requirement.
scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedule_inf.rootCause: Accurate schedule data is the basis for reserve compliance reporting to servicers.
scr_jobcost_reserve_account_schedule_inf.ifSkipped: Reserve compliance reporting to the servicer is inaccurate.

scr_jobcost_job_reporting_codes.purpose: Explains job reporting codes — user-defined codes that group jobs for reporting (e.g., by capital program, fund or year).
scr_jobcost_job_reporting_codes.outcome: Jobs can be reported by program, fund or other groupings.
scr_jobcost_job_reporting_codes.rootCause: Owners review capital by program (e.g., '2026 Value-Add Program'); reporting codes group jobs accordingly without restructuring.
